question: CV Chandrasekhar, recipient of Padma Bhushan is a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CV Chandrasekhar** is one of the most renowned exponents of **Bharatanatyam**, a classical dance form of India.
 
• He is a **recipient of the Padma Bhushan**, the third-highest civilian award in India, in recognition of his immense contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Bharatanatyam is a dance form that originated in **Tamil Nadu** and is known for its intricate footwork, graceful expressions, and emotive storytelling.
 
• CV Chandrasekhar is also an acclaimed **choreographer, teacher, and scholar** in the field of Bharatanatyam, having trained numerous students worldwide.
 
• He has played a significant role in preserving and propagating Bharatanatyam by combining its traditional roots with innovative choreography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• **Origin:** Bharatanatyam originated in **temples of Tamil Nadu** as a form of devotional dance dedicated to the deities, particularly Lord Shiva.
 
• **Components:** The dance integrates **Bhava (expression), Raga (melody), Tala (rhythm), and Natya (dramatic art)**, collectively known as Bharatanatyam.
 
• **Features:** It is characterized by intricate hand gestures (Mudras), rhythmic footwork, elaborate costumes, and facial expressions that convey emotions and stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• **Performances:** Bharatanatyam performances often draw inspiration from texts like the **Natya Shastra** and include themes from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• **Mohiniattam:** Originating in **Kerala**, this dance form is known for its graceful, feminine movements and is often performed as a solo recital by women.
 
• **Kathakali:** A classical dance-drama also from **Kerala**, known for its elaborate costumes, face masks, and storytelling through music and dance.
 
• **Kathak:** Originating in **North India**, Kathak is characterized by its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through facial expressions and hand gestures.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan Award:**
 
 
• It is the **third-highest civilian award** in India, instituted in **1954**, recognizing distinguished service of a high order in any field.
 
• Recipients include individuals from diverse fields such as art, science, public affairs, and sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed in temples as a form of worship and was an integral part of religious rituals.
 
• In the 20th century, pioneers like **Rukmini Devi Arundale** redefined Bharatanatyam as a performance art, bringing it to the global stage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• It serves as a medium for spiritual expression and showcases Indian cultural heritage.
 
• It is one of the **eight recognized classical dance forms** of India as per the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
